sentences.text: 1. Charlie Meadows is hosting a radio show called Brunch with Charlie Listen to the first part of the program and write the information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, ask, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Hi there. How are you doing?
It is Charlie Meadows here again and with me on Brunchwood Charlie this morning are two guests, both from the special committee that has just been set up to find a twin city for Hong Kong.
I’m very pleased to have with me Dr Emily Lee He, who is a member of Legislative Council of Hong Kong.
Welcome Dr Lee.
Good morning, Charlie.
Glad to be here.
And also with me is Lemme Chan.
Hi. Now, Lemme is an undergraduate student at Hong Kong University.
And what is it that you’re studying, Lemme?
Uh, History. Oh yes, history.
I had it noted down somewhere.
somewhere. Now let’s start with you, Dr Lee.
You have been appointed the chairperson of this special committee which has just been set up.
Would you like to tell us about that?
Certainly. Well, as you say it’s a committee set up especially to choose a twin city for Hong Kong.
OK, now a lot of our listeners won’t have heard of the idea of twin cities so maybe Maybe you could explain what it is.
OK, yes, well the other name for a twin city you might have heard of is the sister city.
OK, yes, I’ve heard sister city before yeah.
OK, so when two cities decide they want to be twin cities they enter into an agreement.
And the important thing is that to be twin cities the two cities have to be in different countries.
All right, so not two cities in the same country Yeah that’s right and there are thousands of towns and cities twint with each other across the world OK, so when did this all start then, twin cities?
And why did cities want to twin?
Well, that’s a good question, maybe let me should give a bit of the historical background.
Oh, OK. Well, the idea of twin cities, at least our concept of it in the modern era, started just after World War II.
OK, but why then?
Why were twin Cities so important after the war?
Didn’t people have better things to be doing rebuilding houses and everything?
Well, twin cities were seen as part of a wider initiative at that time to promote peace and understanding.
So it had a serious point to it So does that mean that twin cities were in countries which were fighting each other during the war?
That's right, in countries which were until a couple of years before that fighting each other.
Wow. That can’t have been easy.
So did it work?
Was it successful?
Well, a lot of cities certainly took part.
Obviously during the war many countries had suffered.
On the one side you had Japan, Germany, Italy and on the other you had, like, the United States, the UK, France and the Soviet Union.
And the most common twinning of cities was actually between France and Germany, many, two countries that had been the fiercest of enemies through history.
Why was that?
I’m sure there must be a good reason.
Well I think just on a practical level, these countries are next to each other and so it was easy for them to communicate with each other.
Well that makes sense.
So thinking about nowadays, a city typically pairs up with just one city?
Is that what happens?
Well it all depends.
Usually a small town, you know, of a few thousand people would usually twin with just one other town.
But there are some towns in Europe that are incredibly popular as a twin town.
There's this one town called Judenburg in Austria, and it's twinned with over thirty different towns.

sentences.text: A big city is usually twinned with more than one city, but certainly not thirty.

sentences.text: Say four or five.
Ten would be unusual.
Right, so Hong Kong is now looking for its first twin city, so what do you hope to achieve?
Maybe I could answer this.
The first thing we want to achieve is to encourage an exchange of culture.
An exchange of culture sounds nice.
But what does it mean exactly?
Exactly. Well, the obvious ones are language and food.
I mean Hong Kong has a variety of languages and lots of amazing food that we can share with the future twin city.
Nice! What else?
Well, another aim is related to commerce.
It’s the promotion of business links.
So what kind of business links?
It can be any kind really.
For instance, Hong Kong is really good at banking, I mean obviously, and another area which I find quite exciting is fashion design.
Really? Wow, that’s quite glamorous then.
Yeah, it would be great to be twinned with one of the fashion design capitals of the world.
Yeah, and maybe I could come with you!
Right, we’re going to take a short music break and we'll be back in a couple of minutes.
